To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

inclusive pion double-charge-exchange reactions have been observed at 180 and 200 MeV in /sup 4,6,12/C, /super 16,O, /sup 208,Pb, and /sup Rh103/; and that the reaction cross sections are sensitive to the charge and mass of the target nucleus.
the inclusive pion double-charge-exchange cross sections are strongly dependent on the nuclear charge and mass and that the dependence is explained by a simple phenomenological model.

the total reaction cross section for pion double-charge exchange is approximately proportional to the square of the nuclear mass and approximately proportional to the product of the nuclear charge and the charge of incident pion.

the cross sections for inclusive double charge exchange are dominated by the single-charge-ex-change processes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cross sections for inclusive charge-exchange reactions are dominated by quasifree-scattering processes, and that the contribution from successive single-charge exchanges is a relatively small correction.
, for the nuclei studied, the inclusive double-charge-exchange cross section is a function of the incident pions' charge, the mass of the target nucleus, and the number of nucleons in the nucleus.
the total inclusive double-charge-exchange reaction cross section is a sensitive function of the nuclear charge but is only weakly dependent on nuclear mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the total reaction cross section for pion double charge-exchange can be expressed as the sum of two terms, one of which depends upon the mass of the target nucleus, and the second of which depends upon its charge and the charge of pion.
